issue.title: Lang-SDK runtimes: one transport for native Dag parsing and the task-handler probe
issue.body:
Native Dag parsing (#74035, `LangSDKDagFileProcessorProcess` in `dag_processing/lang_sdk_processor.py`) and the task-handler probe (#73974, `LangSDKTaskHandlerProcessorProcess` in `dag_processing/task_handler_processor.py`) each carry their own copy of the runtime transport: the listeners, connection checks, frame reading, request handling, timeouts and the runtime kill, plus their own `StartLangSDKRuntime` and `LangSDKRuntimeSchemaVersion` models. Once both are on `main`:

- Extract one shared base and move both processes onto it, with a single `tests/unit/dag_processing/fake_lang_sdk.py`.
- Keep that commit free of behaviour changes. Then, as separate changes, give native parsing what the probe already has: a reported start failure (`LangSDKRuntimeStartFailed`), non-blocking frame reads, killing what a runtime leaves behind, and cleanup when a start fails after the fork. The parent-death signal stays opt-in, because a native parse may be started from a short-lived thread.
- Results from a Lang-SDK runtime must not carry `task_handler_bindings` or `probed_artifacts`; the manager ignores those fields from a runtime.

---

Drafted with Claude Code (Opus 5.5).

comments.body: I'd like to investigate and take the first implementation slice here: extract the shared Lang-SDK runtime transport only after confirming the prerequisite parser/task-handler changes on main, with no behavior changes in the refactor. I will use a separate fork branch and add focused transport tests before opening a PR.
